    Model equations

    This guide describes the reactor model implemented by MultiSolid-CL. The equations below use the same concentration bases, face fluxes, boundary conditions, and source-term conventions as PackedBedModel (online). Standard and Compiled execution start from this model; their numerical treatment is described in Time integration.

    The core balances apply to every selected chemistry. Individual kinetic laws and property datasets are supplied by built-in definitions or plugins. Their validity ranges and provenance remain part of those definitions; see Reaction sources.

    Scope and assumptions

    The reactor is a fixed cylindrical bed represented in one axial dimension. Cross-sectional variations are unresolved. The implemented assumptions are:

    • Gas is an ideal mixture. Each cell has one pressure, gas composition, and temperature. Gas and solids share that temperature: local thermal equilibrium is assumed, with no separate gas-to-solid heat-transfer equation.
    • Solids are stationary. Their inventories change through reactions, with no axial solid transport. Gas moves by convection and axial dispersion.
    • Bed radius, bed length, interparticle and intraparticle voidages, and particle diameters are prescribed and remain fixed during a run. Reaction-induced changes in solid inventory do not change voidage or geometry.
    • The gas storage volume can include particle pores, but there is no separate pore-gas state or resolved intraparticle diffusion problem. Particle effects such as an effectiveness factor must be represented by the selected kinetics.
    • The pressure gradient follows an algebraic Ergun closure. There is no momentum accumulation equation, gravity term, or independent prescribed interior flow.
    • Species enthalpies depend on temperature and include their reference enthalpies. Stored energy is internal energy, with ideal-gas pressure-volume correction and negligible solid pressure-volume contribution. Kinetic and gravitational potential energy are omitted.
    • Heat exchange with the environment is represented by a constant overall wall coefficient and ambient temperature. An optional constant axial heat-dispersion coefficient acts on the shared temperature. There is no separate wall energy state, resolved radial conduction, or radiation term.

    These assumptions define the implemented model. In particular, selecting a reaction family does not add a separate particle, wall, or gas-temperature model.

    Notation and grid

    Use SI units unless a particular kinetic correlation explicitly converts them. The gas constant in the implementation is R=8.31446 Jmol−1K−1.

    Symbol Meaning Unit or basis
    L, Rb, A=πRb2 Bed length, radius, cross-sectional area m, m, m²
    j, i, a, k Cell, gas species, solid species, reaction indices —
    eb, ep Interparticle voidage; pore fraction within particles Dimensionless
    εg, εs Modelled gas volume and solid skeleton volume per bed volume Dimensionless
    ci, sa Gas and solid concentrations stored by the model mol/m³ bed
    Ci=ci/εg Gas-phase concentration mol/m³ gas
    ct=∑ici, Ct=ct/εg Total gas concentrations on the two bases mol/m³ bed; mol/m³ gas
    yi=ci/ct Gas mole fraction Dimensionless
    rk, Sig, Sas Reaction-extent rate and species source terms mol/(m³ bed·s)
    uf Superficial gas velocity at a face m/s, based on total area A
    Ni,f Gas species molar flux at a face mol/(m² bed·s)
    hig, has Species molar enthalpies J/mol
    Ji,f, qf Species enthalpy flux; axial dispersive heat flux W/m² bed
    Ej Cell internal energy per bed volume J/m³ bed
    P, T, ρg, μg Gas pressure, shared temperature, gas density, mixture viscosity Pa, K, kg/m³ gas, Pa·s
    Df, dp,f Axial mass-dispersion coefficient; particle diameter m²/s, m
    U, T∞, λax Wall heat-transfer coefficient, ambient temperature, axial heat dispersion W/(m²·K), K, W/(m·K)

    Positive flux is from the inlet at x=0 to the outlet at x=L. Mathematical cell indices here run from 1 to n; Python array indices run from 0 to n−1.

    The configured grid is uniform, with at least three cells:

    Δx=Ln,xj=(j−12)Δx,xj−1/2=(j−1)Δx.

    Concentrations, temperature, pressure, and gas properties live at cell centres. Velocities, particle diameters, dispersion coefficients, and transport fluxes live at faces. Define the conservative cell divergence of a face quantity as

    Dj(F)=Fj+1/2−Fj−1/2Δxj,Δxj=xj+1/2−xj−1/2.

    The balances retain this cell-width form, but the supplied grid builder and higher-order reconstruction formulas use a uniform grid. The distance used in an interior face gradient is xj+1−xj; the inlet and outlet pressure-drop segments are half a cell wide.

    Volume fractions and concentration bases

    The model.gas_voidage_mode setting defines gas storage:

    εg={eb+(1−eb)ep,bed_and_particle (default),eb,bed_only.εs=(1−eb)(1−ep).

    bed_only excludes pore gas from storage while retaining the same solid skeleton fraction. Consequently εg+εs need not equal one in that mode: the excluded pore volume is not reassigned to solids. The chosen gas fraction is used in initialization, the equation of state, transport concentrations, and energy storage. Ergun resistance always uses eb.

    Solids are specified in contiguous zones covering the bed. Zone voidages and initial solid values are sampled at cell centres; a narrow zone containing no cell centre does not contribute a cell inventory. Choose a resolution that represents the intended zones. Particle diameters are sampled at faces. A face exactly on a zone boundary uses the arithmetic mean of the two adjacent zone diameters. These rules are implemented in solid_profiles.py (online).

    Let va be an entered solid value and Ma its molecular weight in kg/mol. The conversion to the model state is

    sa,0=b{va,mol_per_m3,va/Ma,kg_per_m3,b={1,basis: bed,εs,basis: solid.

    Thus a value per solid volume is multiplied by the solid skeleton fraction; mass inputs are divided by molecular weight first. Outputs and reaction source terms continue to use mol/m³ bed regardless of the input basis. No evolving solid-density or volume-filling closure is imposed.

    Species balances and reaction sources

    Gas and solid balances

    For each gas species and cell,

    dci,jdt+Dj(Ni)=Si,jg.

    For each stationary solid species,

    dsa,jdt=Sa,js.

    There is no extra voidage multiplier on these accumulation or source terms: ci, sa, and both sources already use total bed volume. The total concentrations and mole fractions are algebraic closures:

    ct,j=∑ici,j,st,j=∑asa,j,yi,jct,j=ci,j.

    Gas mole fractions sum to one when the total gas concentration is nonzero and the closures are satisfied. Total solid concentration is not held constant.

    Stoichiometric source terms

    Each selected reaction has one extent rate rk,j. Its signed stoichiometric coefficients νikg and νaks are negative for reactants and positive for products:

    Si,jg=∑kνikgrk,j,Sa,js=∑kνaksrk,j.

    The reaction network builds these matrices from the selected definitions in reactions.py (online). Sources from all selected reactions add; selecting two mechanisms for the same conversion does not make one replace the other. With no reactions, all source terms are zero.

    For example, a reaction written as Fe2O3+3H2→2Fe+3H2O gives SH2g=−3r, SH2Og=3r, SFe2O3s=−r, and SFes=2r. The scalar r is an extent rate; the stoichiometric coefficients are applied once by the source matrices. They do not determine kinetic reaction orders.

    A kinetic hook receives the cell state and returns a symbolic rate in mol/(m³ bed·s). A correlation defined per gas volume, catalyst mass, or another basis must perform its own conversion to that output basis. The core model does not automatically multiply hook results by voidage or catalyst loading. Partial pressures follow pi=yiP; correlations using bar or other units must convert from the model's pascals. Catalyst roles can affect a rate without having a stoichiometric source term.

    Clamping, gas-availability gates, conversion limits, and regularization constants belong to individual kinetic implementations. There is no universal reaction-rate clip or limiter that guarantees nonnegative concentrations. Transient solver trial states can leave a correlation's physical domain.

    Family Implementation
    Copper on silica, San Pio form copper_sio2.py (online)
    Copper on alumina, including spinel chemistry copper_al2o3.py (online)
    Nickel redox, Medrano form nickel_medrano.py (online)
    Nickel-catalysed reforming, Xu–Froment form reforming_xu_froment.py (online)
    Nickel-catalysed reforming, Numaguchi–Kikuchi form reforming_numaguchi.py (online)
    Iron redox, He form iron_he.py (online)

    The kinetics source notes identify scientific references and implementation-specific choices. The additional waste iron plugin documents its own rate laws and property fits. Plugin and built-in variants use the same core balances; changing their rates or properties can change both composition and temperature.

    Thermodynamic and transport properties

    Equation of state and density

    The ideal-gas closure is

    Pjεg,j=ct,jRTj,Ct,j=PjRTj.

    With gas molecular weights Mi in kg/mol,

    Mmix,j=∑iyi,jMi,ρg,j=PjMmix,jRTj=∑iCi,jMi.

    This is density per gas volume, as needed by Ergun. Multiplying it by εg gives gas mass per bed volume.

    Species enthalpy and heat capacity

    Every selected gas or solid species supplies h(T). Consistent heat capacity is Cp(T)=dh/dT. Reference enthalpies must use a consistent chemical reference because reaction energy is obtained from these species enthalpies.

    For PolynomialHeatCapacity, with coefficients am and θ=T−Tref,

    Cp(T)=∑m=0pamθm,h(T)=href+∑m=0pamm+1θm+1.

    The coefficients are in ascending powers of T−Tref, not powers of absolute T. The parameter h_form_ref supplies href in J/mol.

    For ShomateHeatCapacity, let T*=1000 K, τ=T/T*, and τref=Tref/T*:

    Cp(T)=a0+a1τ+a2τ2+a3τ3+a4τ−2,
    h(T)=href+T*[&a0(τ−τref)+a12(τ2−τref2)+a23(τ3−τref3)&+a34(τ4−τref4)−a4(τ−1−τref−1)].

    This implementation anchors the integrated heat capacity at the explicitly supplied reference enthalpy; it does not take a separate pair of Shomate enthalpy-offset coefficients. Custom correlations supply numerical and symbolic enthalpy/heat-capacity functions. Scientific validity and agreement between those functions must be established for the chosen temperature range.

    Viscosity

    The built-in pure-species QuadraticViscosity correlation is

    μi(T)=a0,i+a1,i(T−Tref,i)+a2,i(T−Tref,i)2.

    Mixture viscosity uses Wilke's rule:

    μg=∑iyiμi∑ℓyℓϕiℓ,ϕiℓ=[1+μi/μℓ(Mℓ/Mi)1/4]28(1+Mi/Mℓ).

    The diagonal factor is exactly one. The implementation does not divide by mole fractions, so absent species with zero mole fraction are supported when the property values and remaining mixture are valid. Initialization and the evolving model use the same function. See properties.py (online) and the IDAES description of Wilke's rule (online).

    Gas transport and pressure drop

    Interior species fluxes

    At an interior face f=j+1/2,

    Df=12|uf|dp,f,C―t,f=12(ct,jεg,j+ct,j+1εg,j+1),
    Ni,f=Af(uf,Ci)−DfC―t,fyi,j+1−yi,jxj+1−xj.

    Here Af is the scheme-dependent convective transport operator defined in Spatial reconstruction. The dispersed gradient is mole fraction, multiplied by the arithmetic face mean of total gas-phase concentration. It is not the gradient of concentration per bed volume.

    The mass-dispersion coefficient is common to the gas species and contains no separate molecular-diffusion term. It vanishes at zero velocity. The dispersive species fluxes sum to zero when both neighbouring compositions sum to one. The boundary species fluxes are prescribed separately below; the interior formula is not evaluated across an external ghost cell.

    Ergun closure

    Define the drag function

    Ef(u)=150μf(1−eb,f)2eb,f3dp,f2u+1.75ρf(1−eb,f)eb,f3dp,f|u|u.

    For each interior face,

    Pj−Pj+1xj+1−xj=Ef(uf).

    Viscosity, density, and interparticle voidage at an interior face are arithmetic means of the adjacent cell values. Particle diameter follows the face-sampling rule above. Boundary drag uses the adjacent cell's viscosity, density, and interparticle voidage.

    The signed |u|u term permits either velocity sign. Velocity and pressure are solved together with species and energy accumulation; total molar flow need not remain equal to the inlet flow along a reacting, transient bed. The interior_flow_mode setting changes transport reconstruction, not this pressure-drop equation.

    Energy balance

    Stored internal energy

    The differential energy state is

    Ej=∑ici,jhig(Tj)+∑asa,jhas(Tj)−εg,jPj.

    The subtraction is the ideal-gas pressure-volume contribution per bed volume. Using the equation of state, the same definition is

    Ej=∑ici,j[hig(Tj)−RTj]+∑asa,jhas(Tj).

    Temperature is recovered through this algebraic relation and the species enthalpy closures. It is shared by gas and solids. Holding the gas and solid concentrations fixed, the derivative of this stored energy with respect to temperature is ∑ici(Cp,ig−R)+∑asaCp,as.

    Enthalpy transport and axial heat dispersion

    At an interior face, the enthalpy flux of gas species i is

    Ji,f=Af(Ni,f,hig),Hf=∑iJi,f.

    This uses the complete species molar flux, including its dispersive part. The heat_scheme reconstructs each species enthalpy. In reversible mode, its upwind direction follows the sign of that species flux, which need not be the same as the sign of superficial velocity.

    The additional axial heat flux is

    qf=−λaxTj+1−Tjxj+1−xjat interior faces,q1/2=qn+1/2=0.

    The constant model.axial_heat_dispersion_w_per_m_k is nonnegative and defaults to zero. The coefficient and heat flux use the total bed cross section; no additional gas or solid volume fraction multiplies this expression. This term can conduct heat at zero flow and is independent of the velocity-dependent mass-dispersion coefficient.

    Wall exchange and cell balance

    The volumetric heat loss to the surroundings is

    Qwall,j=2URb(Tj−T∞).

    The factor 2/Rb is the cylindrical sidewall-area-to-bed-volume ratio. Positive Qwall removes energy; it becomes a heat input when the surroundings are hotter. The model uses one constant U and one T∞ for the whole bed.

    The energy equation is

    dEjdt+Dj(H)+Dj(q)+Qwall,j=0.

    When λax=0, the heat-dispersion divergence is omitted. Internal face heat transfers enter neighbouring cells with opposite signs. Since dispersive heat flux is zero at both boundaries, this term redistributes stored energy without providing an external heat source.

    How reaction heat enters

    There is no additional −ΔHrr term in the solved energy balance. Reactions change the species inventories, and the stored energy includes those species' reference and sensible enthalpies. Adding a second reaction-heat source to this formulation would count the same contribution twice.

    To see the connection, define

    Cp,bed,j=∑ici,jCp,ig(Tj)+∑asa,jCp,as(Tj),ΔHk(T)=∑iνikghig(T)+∑aνakshas(T).

    Differentiating the energy definition at fixed voidage and substituting the species balances gives the equivalent identity

    Cp,bed,jdTjdt−εg,jdPjdt=&−Dj(H)−Dj(q)−Qwall,j&+∑ihig(Tj)Dj(Ni)−∑kΔHk(Tj)rk,j.

    This identity explains the implicit reaction heat and pressure correction; it is not an extra equation assembled by the solver. The implementation integrates Ej directly. In particular, storing total enthalpy instead of Ej would omit the pressure contribution during transients.

    Boundary conditions

    The operating program prescribes total inlet molar flow Fin(t)>0, inlet composition yi,in(t), inlet temperature Tin(t), and outlet pressure Pout(t). Inlet pressure is solved, not supplied independently.

    Inlet

    Ni,1/2=FinAyi,in,Ji,1/2=Ni,1/2hig(Tin),q1/2=0.

    The inlet velocity and pressure obey

    FinA=u1/2PinRTin,Pin−P1x1−0=E1/2(u1/2).

    This is a prescribed total species-flux and enthalpy-flux boundary. The first cell's composition and temperature are not fixed to the inlet values during integration. No additional species dispersion flux is added to the prescribed Ni,1/2.

    Outlet

    Ni,n+1/2=un+1/2ci,nεg,n,Ji,n+1/2=Ni,n+1/2hig(Tn),qn+1/2=0,
    Pn−PoutL−xn=En+1/2(un+1/2).

    Outlet species and enthalpy fluxes use the final cell directly, with no added axial species-dispersion flux. There is no independently imposed outlet composition or temperature. Solids have no boundary flux at either end.

    Flow reversal limits

    simulation.interior_flow_mode: reversible switches interior reconstruction according to flux direction. Both inlet and outlet equations above remain unchanged. There is no external outlet-reservoir composition or temperature to supply a physical backflow boundary. Reversible interior transport should therefore not be interpreted as a model of interchangeable inlet/outlet ports.

    forward_only always uses the forward-oriented face reconstruction. It does not clamp negative velocity or remove the signed Ergun closure; cases with interior reversal require the reversible reconstruction.

    Operating programs

    Programs consist of an initial value and timed hold or ramp steps. A hold keeps the preceding value; a ramp has an absolute target. Channels without steps remain constant. Flow, temperature, and pressure inputs are positive; each specified composition includes every selected gas species and sums to one.

    Separate channels and feed streams

    In separate_channels mode, flow, temperature, composition, and outlet pressure are independently programmed. In feed_stream mode, the inlet program instead interpolates the molar quantities

    F,Gi=Fyi,B=FT.

    After interpolation and smoothing,

    yi,in(t)=Gi(t)F(t),Tin(t)=B(t)F(t).

    All inlet quantities use the same positive flow denominator. This preserves species molar-flow interpolation when the total flow changes. The temperature is weighted by molar flow, not by an enthalpy balance between two feed streams. A ramp target may omit flow, temperature, or composition; omitted values carry forward from the preceding feed. Outlet pressure remains a separate channel.

    Ramp smoothing

    The default smoothing half-width is w=1 s. Define the smoothed positive part of elapsed time z by

    gw(z)={0,z≤−w,(z+w)2/(4w),−w<z<w,z,z≥w.

    A ramp from a to b between ts and te contributes

    (b−a)gw(t−ts)−gw(t−te)te−ts

    to the carried value. Each corner is smoothed only within w of its endpoint; outside those regions, the result agrees with the unsmoothed piecewise-linear program. If short steps have overlapping smoothing regions, the same summed formula applies. Values and first derivatives are continuous at the joins.

    For feed streams the smoothing is applied to F, Gi, and B before taking ratios. A ramp starting at time zero can therefore alter the actual inlet state at t=0 from its declared initial values. Initialization, previews, and both solver backends use these smoothed conditions. The smoothing width is an engine parameter, not a field in the current YAML schema.

    With repeat_program: true, each channel's next cycle starts from its previous cycle's final value; it does not reset to the initial value. The first cycle and the carried-forward continuation are retained, and extending the simulation horizon does not change earlier program values. Repeating channels use their own step-list durations. For non-repeating inputs, each channel with steps must span the configured horizon; channels without steps remain constant.

    GHSV conversion

    When the flow basis is ghsv_per_h, the volumetric flow uses the empty bed volume Vb=AL and the reference conditions TN=273.15 K, PN=100000 Pa:

    Fin=GHSV3600VbPNRTN.

    No voidage factor multiplies Vb. This conversion is shared by both program modes. Program construction is implemented in programs.py (online).

    Initial conditions

    initialization.py (online) constructs the starting state before DAETools solves for consistency:

    1. Build the uniform axial grid, sample the solid zones, convert solid inputs to mol/m³ bed, and calculate the fixed volume fractions and face diameters.
    2. Evaluate the smoothed programs at zero to obtain F0, yi,0, T0, and Pout,0. The initializer requires positive inlet flow.
    3. Evaluate the mixture properties at T0 and yi,0. Construct a positive-flow Ergun pressure-profile seed using the inlet molar flux F0/A, face properties, and half-cell boundary distances. Bracket and bisect the inlet pressure until the constructed outlet pressure matches Pout,0.
    4. Set every cell's initial temperature and gas composition to T0 and yi,0, while allowing pressure and gas concentration to vary axially:
    ci,j(0)=yi,0εg,jPj(0)RT0,sa,j(0)=sa,0,j,
    Ej(0)=∑ici,j(0)hig(T0)+∑asa,j(0)has(T0)−εg,jPj(0).

    Gas and solid concentrations and internal energy are supplied as differential initial conditions. Pressure, temperature, fluxes, rates, and other algebraic quantities receive initial guesses. DAETools' SolveInitial() then obtains consistent algebraic values and differential derivatives before either backend integrates. The pressure construction is an initial-state calculation, not a claim that the reactive bed is initially at steady state or chemical equilibrium. There is no independently specified axial initial gas-composition or temperature profile in the current case format.

    Cumulative inlet/outlet mass and energy transfers and cumulative wall heat loss start at zero. Initial bed inventories are calculated from the initialized concentrations and internal energy.

    Spatial reconstruction

    simulation.mass_scheme and simulation.heat_scheme independently select how interior face states are reconstructed. Species convection reconstructs Ci=ci/εg; enthalpy transport reconstructs hig(T).

    For a generic cell quantity v, let vfL and vfR be reconstructions from the left and right. For signed transport rate af,

    Af(af,v)={afvfL,forward_only,af+vfL+af−vfR,reversible,af±=af±|af|2.

    Use af=uf for species convection and af=Ni,f for species enthalpy transport. Right reconstructions apply the same formulas to the reversed cell sequence. Central reconstruction is identical from either direction.

    Upwind, central, and limited linear schemes

    At the face between cells j and j+1, the left reconstructions are:

    Scheme vfL
    upwind1 vj
    central (vj+vj+1)/2
    linear_upwind2 3vj/2−vj−1/2
    muscl_minmod vj+minmod(vj−vj−1,vj+1−vj)/2

    The limiter returns the argument of smaller magnitude if both differences have the same sign and zero otherwise. At the first interior face, schemes needing a second upstream cell fall back to upwind1.

    WENO3

    For vj−1,vj,vj+1, the candidate states and smoothness indicators are

    p0=32vj−12vj−1,p1=12(vj+vj+1),β0=(vj−vj−1)2,β1=(vj+1−vj)2.

    With d0=1/3, d1=2/3,

    αm=dm(βm+ϵ2)2,ωm=αm∑ℓαℓ,vfL=∑mωmpm.

    WENO5

    For vj−2,vj−1,vj,vj+1,vj+2,

    p0&=13vj−2−76vj−1+116vj,p1&=−16vj−1+56vj+13vj+1,p2&=13vj+56vj+1−16vj+2,
    β0&=1312(vj−2−2vj−1+vj)2+14(vj−2−4vj−1+3vj)2,β1&=1312(vj−1−2vj+vj+1)2+14(vj−1−vj+1)2,β2&=1312(vj−2vj+1+vj+2)2+14(3vj−4vj+1+vj+2)2.

    Use the same nonlinear-weight formula with (d0,d1,d2)=(0.1,0.6,0.3). Where its full stencil is unavailable, weno5 falls back to weno3; where the WENO3 upstream stencil is unavailable, it falls back to upwind1. The same boundary fallback rules apply to the reversed right reconstruction.

    The regularization scale is ϵ=10−8 mol/m3 for gas-phase concentration and 10−8 J/mol for enthalpy. It enters as ϵ2 in the smoothness denominator. It is a reconstruction parameter, not a concentration floor or a solver absolute tolerance.

    These formulas, including their boundary fallbacks, are in axial_schemes.py (online). Higher-order reconstruction and central transport do not guarantee positive concentrations. Mass and heat dispersion continue to use centred differences regardless of the selected convective reconstruction.

    Time integration

    The spatial balances and algebraic closures form a differential-algebraic system F(t,z,z˙)=0. Gas and solid inventories and internal energy are differential states; optional cumulative balance reports add differential accounting states. Fluxes, composition closures, pressure, properties, and reaction rates are algebraic quantities in the unreduced model.

    • Standard (solver.backend: daetools): DAETools assembles and integrates the model using IDAS and the selected linear-solver adapter.
    • Compiled (solver.backend: compiled): DAETools first solves the same initial conditions. The backend exports the equations, substitutes explicit algebraic definitions, eliminates fixed states where applicable, and generates native residuals, analytic Jacobians, and report reconstruction. SUNDIALS IDA integrates the reduced system with SuperLU, KLU, or Band.

    The intended physical balances and boundary conditions are shared. Algebraic elimination changes the solver state vector and error control, so identical settings do not imply bitwise-identical trajectories. See simulation.py (online), the compiled backend (online), and its graph reduction (online).

    IDA uses variable-step, variable-order backward differentiation, with orders from one to five. Its error weights have the form

    Wℓ=1rtol|zℓ|+atolℓ.

    The resulting weighted error norm controls local integration error, not a bound on the error in a final scientific result. The numerical method is described in the SUNDIALS IDA mathematical reference (online).

    solver.concentration_absolute_tolerance sets the gas and solid concentration tolerances in mol/m³ bed; the total-concentration closures use the same types. Other variable types retain their own tolerances. Absolute tolerance is particularly important for trace species, where the relative term is small. maximum_order, nonlinear convergence controls, and suppress_algebraic_errors affect solver behaviour, not the physical source terms. Suppressing algebraic error estimates does not remove the algebraic equations. Compiled residual scaling likewise changes numerical conditioning while retaining the residual zeros.

    reporting_interval_s sets saved output times, not a fixed integration step. The reporting schedule includes zero and the final horizon, adding a shorter last reporting interval if needed. Selecting plots does not change the balances. Selecting mass/heat balance reports adds their accounting equations and can therefore affect the numerical path even though the physical reactor equations are unchanged.

    Conservation diagnostics and reported quantities

    Mass accounting

    The optional mass_balance report stores

    Mbed=A∑jΔxj(∑iMici,j+∑aMasa,j),
    dMindt=A∑iMiNi,1/2,dMoutdt=A∑iMiNi,n+1/2.

    Its signed reported error is

    δM=Mbed(t)−Mbed(0)−Min(t)+Mout(t).

    Summing cell balances cancels the interior fluxes exactly at the equation level. Zero physical mass error also requires each selected reaction to satisfy ∑iMiνikg+∑aMaνaks=0 with the actual selected molecular weights. A nonzero diagnostic can therefore reflect stoichiometry/property inconsistency as well as numerical error. The core source assembly does not repair an unbalanced reaction.

    Energy accounting

    The optional heat_balance report stores

    Ebed=A∑jΔxjEj,dQindt=AH1/2,dQoutdt=AHn+1/2,dQlossdt=A∑jΔxjQwall,j.

    Its signed reported error is

    δE=Ebed(t)−Ebed(0)−Qin(t)+Qout(t)+Qloss(t).

    Despite the output name heat_bed_total, the stored inventory is internal energy. heat_in_total and heat_out_total accumulate boundary enthalpy transfer. Axial dispersive heat contributes no boundary transfer, and reaction heat is already included through the species enthalpies. The cumulative quantities are integrated as part of the DAE, not estimated afterwards by trapezoidal integration of saved samples. All transfers retain their signs.

    These diagnostics are reported in kg and J. The summary identifies the largest absolute error among saved reporting times, not necessarily its largest value between those times. Good conservation alone does not establish accurate kinetics, adequate spatial resolution, or valid property data.

    Interpreting derived outputs

    reports.py (online) derives the following quantities from the retained model data:

    • Outlet temperature is the last cell's temperature, Tn.
    • Pressure drop is Pin−Pout, including both boundary half-cell segments.
    • Outlet species flow is ANi,n+1/2 and total outlet flow is its sum.
    • Outlet composition is Ni,n+1/2/∑ℓNℓ,n+1/2. When the magnitude of the total outlet flux is at most 10−12 mol/(m2s), the reported composition falls back to the final-cell mole fractions.
    • Solid mole fraction is sa/∑bsb when total solid concentration is positive; an empty solid inventory reports zero fractions. This is a derived quantity, not an additional dynamic state or a solid volume fraction.

    For numerical comparisons, vary the axial grid and solver tolerances, compare both conservation errors and quantities of interest, and retain the selected chemistry and property definitions with the results.
